comment: Never-worse ratchet: the gate fails when the problem count is HIGHER than this, and never on errors alone. Was 103 before the 1.0.6 review cleanup. Of the 22 left, 14 are in two files nobody can usefully fix -- 12 in src/kaitai/rmv6-generated.js (machine-generated; hand edits are lost on the next `npm run generate:kaitai`) and 2 in src/shims/setimmediate.ts (a bundle polyfill, where `globalThis` and a bare `setTimeout` are correct and Obsidian's popout-window rules do not apply). The other 11 are in src/main.ts: 8 are the deprecated imperative settings API (`display`, `setWarning`) -- DELIBERATE: the replacement needs Obsidian 1.13.0, which is Catalyst early-access only, so adopting it would restrict the plugin to paying insiders; revisit when 1.13 ships publicly. 1 is `settings-tab/prefer-setting-definitions` on `TaggedSyncSettingTab`, which appeared on 2026-08-09 with the local-model settings and raised this number from 10 -- the SAME 1.13.0 tradeoff seen from the class rather than the call: `getSettingDefinitions()` is the API those 8 warnings point at, so it is one decision, not two, and it lifts when they do. 1 is a `ui/sentence-case` false positive on the feature-voting settings entry, where the anchor text "existing requests" sits mid-sentence and must stay lowercase. 1 is `prefer-file-manager-trash-file` on the `vault.trash(file, true)` that crop cleanup deletes through -- DELIBERATE for the same reason from the other side: `FileManager.trashFile()` needs Obsidian 1.6.6 while manifest.json declares minAppVersion 1.5.7, so calling it trips `no-unsupported-api`, which is an error, and the rule cannot be disabled inline (`eslint-comments/no-restricted-disable`). Raising minAppVersion would drop real users on 1.5.7-1.6.5 to satisfy a style preference; revisit when the floor moves past 1.6.6. It rose from 11 to 13 on 2026-08-09 when the OpenAI-compatible adapter and its Ollama/LM Studio vision probes moved from pro/ into src/ for the free localhost backend (free-localhost-ocr spec §2): both carry a `fetchFn ?? fetch` default, which src/fetch-shim.ts names as one of the two patterns esbuild's inject exists to rewrite -- so the identifier IS requestUrl at run time and the warning describes source, not behaviour. pro/ is not linted, which is why the same two lines cost nothing before the move. Not silenced: eslint-comments/no-restricted-disable forbids disabling no-restricted-globals inline. Lower this number whenever you fix something; nothing forces it down. Re-measure with `node scripts/release-checks.mjs lint --write`. It rose from 11 to 17 on 2026-08-14 with Tagged Sync Pro, and the composition today is: 11 `no-deprecated`, all in src/main.ts and all the same 1.13.0 tradeoff described above -- the Pro section, the trial button and the licence-key field each re-render through `display()` after they change something, so they are that one decision seen three more times and they lift when it does; 3 `no-restricted-globals`, the third now on `fetch` in src/licence-client.ts, which is the pattern src/fetch-shim.ts exists to rewrite -- the identifier IS requestUrl at run time, esbuild's inject makes it so, and it cannot be silenced inline for the reason already given; 2 `ui/sentence-case`, the new one on the heading `Tagged Sync Pro`, a product name the rule cannot know about, same class of false positive as the anchor text; and 1 `prefer-setting-definitions`, unchanged. pro/ IS linted from this date -- it was published, so `eslint .` reaches it, and leaving it on the ignore list would have made the paid source the one source nobody checks. Linting it for the first time surfaced FOUR ERRORS, which were fixed in the same commit rather than baselined: three unnecessary type assertions that TypeScript had outgrown, and one real defect -- an `async` callback passed to `window.setTimeout`, so a vision probe that threw escaped as an unhandled rejection and left the settings row reading "Checking…" for good. It now maps a throw onto the `partial` verdict, which is the branch that already existed for exactly that case. pro/ contributes 3 of the 20 warnings: 2 `no-restricted-globals` on `fetch`, the same inject pattern as the three in src/, and 1 `ui/sentence-case` on "OpenAI-compatible", a brand name the rule cannot know. It rose from 20 to 25 on 2026-08-24 with the direct-device transport, and all five are the SAME `no-deprecated` on `display()`, in src/settings-tab.ts: the source picker, the fallback picker, "Re-pair", "Forget device" and the pairing attempt each re-render the tab after they change something, which is the only way to redraw a row under the pre-1.13.0 settings API. That is the 1.13.0 tradeoff described above seen five more times, not a new decision, and all five lift the day `getSettingDefinitions()` is reachable without restricting the plugin to Catalyst insiders. The `no-deprecated` count is therefore 16 and the rest of the composition is unchanged: 5 `no-restricted-globals` on `fetch` (the src/fetch-shim.ts inject pattern), 3 `ui/sentence-case` false positives on product and brand names, 1 `prefer-setting-definitions`.
